question.problem:
Find the median of the random variable $X$ if the probability density function of $X$ is given by

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14158151/assets/e3eb6147bfde4d3e4c65bad5054fc311cf561c1c869530bbf693f362a057033d.svg)
question.worked_solution:
The median of a random variable $X$ is the number $m$ such that

$$
P(X \leq m) = \dfrac{1}{2}.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le m) & ={\int }_{1}^{m}\frac{2}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}|}_{1}^{m} \\  & =-\frac{1}{{m}^{2}}+1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the median is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{{m}^{2}}+1 & =\frac{1}{2} \\ \frac{1}{{m}^{2}} & =\frac{1}{2} \\ m & =\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we took the positive root because $m \geq 1.$
